name: Main Street Mornington Festival
tagline: Mornington’s big street-festival day - food, wine, music and Main Street closed to traffic.
summary: Main Street Mornington Festival is the town’s broadest community street festival: local food, wine, beer, cider, produce, craft, music, kids’ activities and roving performers along Mornington’s main village spine. It has historically run on the third Sunday in October. It did not run in 2025, and the organisers cancelled the 2026 edition on 11 August 2026 over funding. Check the organiser before you plan travel around it.
recurrence: Annual when funded. Cancelled in 2025 and 2026.
heroImageAlt: Local produce and market stalls on the Mornington Peninsula
whatItIs:
A free, family-friendly street festival staged along Main Street Mornington, combining local food and wine, craft beer and cider, market stalls, local produce, music, kids’ activities and street performance. The organiser describes it as an annual event traditionally held on the third Sunday in October, with multiple stages and performance areas and a large day-visitor crowd.

The caveat matters, and it has grown. The 2025 edition was cancelled, and on 11 August 2026 Northern Mornington Peninsula Tourism cancelled 2026 as well, saying it could not secure the level of funding needed to make the event financially viable. The organisers said they will keep reviewing opportunities for the future. This page therefore documents the festival as part of the Peninsula calendar, not as a confirmed current-year listing.
whoItsFor: Families, local residents, Mornington day-trippers, market browsers and visitors who want a low-barrier Peninsula day without ticketing or a formal itinerary. It is best approached as a whole-town street day: wander, eat, watch a set, walk down to the foreshore, then decide whether to stay for dinner.
peninsulaCalendarContext: Gives Mornington a spring civic anchor, distinct from the wine-country weekends in Red Hill and the summer events at Portsea. It belongs in the Signature Events mix because it uses the town itself as the venue and pulls together food, wine, music, craft and family programming in one walkable strip.
gettingThere: Mornington is the easiest of the major Peninsula towns to reach from Melbourne: usually 60–75 minutes in clear traffic via Peninsula Link. On festival days, expect road closures around Main Street and use foreshore or edge-of-centre parking, then walk in. The event pairs naturally with Mornington Pier, the foreshore and dinner in town.
editorialNotes: 2025 cancelled; 2026 cancelled 11 August 2026 (Mornington Peninsula News) over a funding shortfall. Traditional timing third Sunday October, 11am to 5pm. No 2027 commitment from the organisers. Keep visible copy cautious and do not restore a current-year date until the organiser announces one. Source: https://www.mpnews.com.au/2026/08/11/main-street-mornington-festival-cancelled-for-2026/
